clue.text: Collapsed, having lost spark in performance

indicators.note: in tells us the flat piece sits inside the word for performance

parts.note: a deed is an act or performance
something that has lost its sparkle or fizz is flat

explanation.surface: A performer gave a lifeless show and slumped afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyre or balloon that has collapsed has had its air let out, the literal sense of the word.

clue.text: Governess expected to get girl set up

parts.note: due means expected, as in the train is due

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the girl's name is written upwards, i.e. reversed

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A governess is anticipated to find a girl a position.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone or older woman in charge of girls, especially in Spain or Portugal.

clue.text: Quite an insect that seems to have breathed!

indicators.note: seems to have says the insect has taken something into itself

parts.note: a fly is an insect
something that has breathed has drawn in air

explanation.surface: An exclamation that an insect looks as if it has taken a breath.
explanation.walkthrough: The insect 'has breathed', so it holds AIR inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairly and quite both mean moderately, to some degree, as in quite good.

clue.text: A very quiet ramble daughter agreed to

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quiet
to rove is to wander or ramble

explanation.surface: A daughter consented to a hushed country walk.
explanation.definitionFit: To have approved something is to have consented or given it the go-ahead.

clue.text: Jazz singer offers uplifting 'Alleluia', not half!

indicators.note: uplifting in a down clue means the letters read upwards, i.e. reversed
not half drops half the word, leaving its first four letters

explanation.surface: A jazz vocalist performs a rousing hymn of praise, but only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' is British slang for 'very much', but here it cuts Alleluia in half.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella Fitzgerald, the celebrated American jazz vocalist.

clue.text: Little son worries — sudden attacks of fear

parts.note: S is the usual short form of son
cares are worries or anxieties

explanation.surface: A small boy frets and suffers bouts of panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden frights or panics are synonyms, as in a health scare.

clue.text: Singer from Merseyside area

definitions.meaning: a coastal town north of Liverpool on Merseyside

explanation.surface: A vocalist who comes from the Liverpool region.
explanation.walkthrough: Merseyside is the county around Liverpool in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bing of White Christmas fame shares his surname with a seaside town near Liverpool.

clue.text: Characters in riot fret about something modern being introduced

indicators.note: about says the letters of riot fret are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: People in a riot worry about something new arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters in' points to the letters of riot fret as the material to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding newer parts or equipment to an older machine or building after manufacture.

clue.text: Academic course seems terrible? Cut period of learning!

indicators.note: terrible says the letters of seems are badly jumbled
cut means the last letter is chopped off the period word

parts.note: a term is a period of study at school

explanation.surface: A student complains a course is awful and should be shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges SEEMS into SEMES; 'Cut' takes the M off TERM, leaving TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-year teaching period at a college or university, used especially in the US.

clue.text: Way-out assessment at election time

parts.note: a survey of voters taken as they leave the polling station, so literally on the way out

explanation.surface: An eccentric, way-out judgement made during an election campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way-out' reads as 'weird', but it is literal: voters are questioned as they walk out of the polling station.
explanation.definitionFit: This survey of voters leaving the booths gives an early forecast of the result on polling day.

clue.text: Base character in Shakespeare play

definitions.meaning: the base or lowest part of something
Nick, the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A lowly role in a Shakespeare drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The underside or foot of a thing; also the weaver given an ass's head in the Dream.

clue.text: Look at contrary boy creating shame

parts.note: to scan is to look at closely

indicators.note: contrary means turned the other way, so the boy word reads backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Examine a perverse youngster who is causing disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: A public disgrace or outrage brings dishonour, i.e. ignominy.

clue.text: One dying in his ship's hold

definitions.meaning: Admiral Horatio ... died aboard his flagship HMS Victory at Trafalgar
a wrestling grip applied from behind, under the opponent's arms

explanation.surface: A sailor meets his end in the cargo space of his own vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' looks like the cargo space of the ship; it is a wrestling grip, and the 's is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The admiral died aboard Victory; a full or half wrestling grip also carries his name.

clue.text: Plant coming from Cuba is so unusual

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of Cuba and is so are set out in an uncommon new order

explanation.surface: A flower from the Caribbean island is rare.
explanation.definitionFit: A wildflower with pincushion-like blue or lilac heads, common in meadows.

clue.text: Fair had success after being set up very recently

indicators.note: after puts the reversed piece behind the fair word

parts.note: just means fair or equitable

indicators.note: being set up in a down clue means written upwards, i.e. reversed

parts.note: won means had success or came first

explanation.surface: A fair-minded person triumphed after things were rigged, a moment ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning a moment ago, a short time back.

clue.text: Five children in the Home Counties getting glittery little bits

parts.note: SE, the South East of England, where the Home Counties around London lie
quins are quintuplets, five children born together

explanation.surface: A family with quintuplets in the commuter belt are bought sparkly trinkets.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in the South East (SE) of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Spangles sewn on clothing are small shiny discs that catch the light.

clue.text: Leader falling off step — one on the floor?

indicators.note: the leader, the first letter, drops away from the step word

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps for climbing over a fence

explanation.surface: Someone at the front stumbles off a step and lands on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: A stile is a step or steps for getting over a fence in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceramic square laid as flooring is one piece among many on a floor, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Ward nurse perhaps bringing glass, interrupted by doctor turning up

indicators.note: interrupted by places the doctor piece in the middle of the glass word

parts.note: a beaker is a drinking glass or cup

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the doctor's letters read upwards, i.e. reversed

parts.note: MD, Doctor of Medicine

explanation.surface: A hospital nurse brings a glass and is interrupted by a doctor arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' looks like arriving; it reverses MD to DM.
explanation.definitionFit: A ward nurse is one example of someone who makes up beds, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Knight or a pair of knights in French headgear?

indicators.note: in puts the article and knights inside the French cap

parts.note: a beret is a soft flat cap associated with France
N is the chess notation for knight, so two give NN

explanation.surface: A knight, or two of them, wearing berets.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval knight who led his own vassals under his own banner.

clue.text: Get in row, stupidly looking down on others?

indicators.note: stupidly says the letters of get in row are arranged foolishly in a new order

explanation.surface: Join a queue foolishly while feeling superior to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something very tall rises high above its surroundings, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Man desperate for food taking some of the sausages

indicators.note: taking some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hungry man helps himself to a few of the bangers.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis this man sold his birthright to his brother Jacob for a meal of stew.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical figure was so hungry he traded his inheritance for a bowl of pottage.

clue.text: Chemical in an hotel getting sprayed

indicators.note: getting sprayed says the letters of an hotel are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A substance in a hotel is being sprayed around.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethyl alcohol is the chemical compound found in drinks and fuel.

clue.text: Loud performer that has to be taken into account

definitions.text: that has to be taken into account

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical mark for loud
an actor is a performer

explanation.surface: A noisy player is someone you must reckon with.
explanation.definitionFit: A consideration or element that influences a result and must be considered.

clue.text: Female learner and relation in parade

parts.note: L is for learner, as on British L-plates
an aunt is a relation

explanation.surface: A woman, a student driver and a relative take part in a procession.
explanation.walkthrough: L-plates mark a learner driver in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To parade something is to show it off ostentatiously.

clue.text: Garment on middle of bench pinched

parts.note: a stole is a scarf or wrap worn over the shoulders

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letter of bench

explanation.surface: A scarf left on the seat has been nicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinched is informal for taken without permission.

clue.text: Fellow finally achieved an eminence as issuer of orders

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of achieved

parts.note: an gives the article A
a tor is a rocky hill or eminence, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A man finally reached high rank as the one giving commands.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop, a term familiar from Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: One who mandates or commands; the word comes from the Latin for command.

clue.text: Fervent enthusiast gets to laze around

indicators.note: around says the letters of to laze are moved about into another order

explanation.surface: A keen fan is allowed to lounge around.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanatic or zealous supporter, named after an ancient Jewish faction.

clue.text: Feature on map indicated by blue or red pigment

definitions.text: Feature on map indicated by blue
definitions.meaning: a body of inland water, coloured blue on maps

explanation.surface: A cartographer's symbol is shown in one colour or the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue or red' looks like a choice of colour; the 'or' only separates the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: An inland body of water appears blue on a map; the word also names a deep red dye.

clue.text: Shrew in need of taming interrupted by a king in unarmed combat

indicators.note: interrupted by places the next pieces in the middle of the shrew's name

parts.note: Kate is the shrew in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered woman, still untamed, is stopped by a monarch in a bare-handed bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrew' looks like a small animal or any scold; here it is Shakespeare's Kate in particular.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese martial art using hands and feet rather than weapons.

clue.text: Inveterate and bluff king keeps somewhat unfriendly at first

indicators.note: keeps means the king's name holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Bluff King Hal is a nickname for Henry VIII
a bit means somewhat, as in a bit tired

indicators.note: first here takes the opening letters of both unfriendly and at

explanation.surface: A hearty monarch who is a little cold from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bluff King Hal' is the traditional nickname of Henry VIII of England. 'first' takes the heads of 'unfriendly at', giving UA.
explanation.definitionFit: An inveterate habit is long ingrained and constant, i.e. regular and customary.

clue.text: Hesitation about stage act coming back

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the hesitation word reads backwards

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
a turn is a performer's act on stage

explanation.surface: A pause before a performer's routine comes round again.
explanation.definitionFit: A coming back to a place or state, as in a journey home.

clue.text: Raise bird for laying eggs with number inside

indicators.note: inside says the number goes within the bird

parts.note: a hen is the farm bird kept for eggs
eight is a number

explanation.surface: Rear a laying bird with a number tag inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to increase or intensify it, make it higher.
